Token --ink. body background, tray, inputs, board-cell. DOUBLE DUTY: also used 16x file-wide as `color` for dark text on amber/maple fills (.confirm-btn, .btn-primary, .slot.filled, .slot-badge, .ls-token, .ls-pos, .ls-swap.is-moving/.is-here, .startover-btn, .tab.on, .cap-info) = accent-ink job. Those uses should point at --t-accent-ink, or a light-ground theme turns amber-button text light.
Token --tunnel. Card/ticket/board/player-row/search fill. Also used once as text on amber (.sort-chip.active color) = accent-ink job.

Token --tunnel-2. File-wide it is used ~21x as a BORDER (player-row, pick-card, ledger, slot, tab, site-foot rule) vs ~7x as a fill (player-row:active/.sel, tw-track, five-chip) and once as an SVG stroke (.rail-path). Border uses are really `line`; the tokenizer should route border uses to --t-line or a line-on-dark theme will repaint wells too.
Token --chalk. Primary text on dark (body color, 43 color uses).
Token --chalk-dim. Secondary/dim text (54 color uses), placeholder text.

Token --maple. Ornament bronze: 3px ticket/board top rules, pips, focus borders. Also used as TEXT (16x: .eyebrow, .pr-pos, .chip, .pro-hint, .year-sel, .cap-season, footer stats) and as FILL behind ink text (.slot-badge, .slot.filled, .tab.on, .ls-token, .climb-pin, .round-pips .done). A theme that repaints metal repaints all eyebrow labels too.
Token --maple-line. Plain 1-2px rules/borders on dark (site-head, tray top, ticket, board, chips, inputs, cap-bar). One non-rule use: hard 3px text-shadow extrusion under .kaman-big.

Token --amber. Brand amber: primary fills (.confirm-btn, .btn-primary, .sort-chip.active), key numbers (.pr-v, .board .big, .ticket-dec), focus outlines, rings. 61 color + 21 background uses file-wide.
Token --whistle. Negative values: ledger tax, weak tier, warn stats, .error-box border, .tw-nub, strike-through old price.
Token --ok. Positive values: ledger zero/good/hot, good stats, fire-sale new price.

notes: Literal count: grep for hex/rgb()/rgba()/hsl() over styles.css lines 1-1100 finds 97. Entries = 98: the extra one is %23B98A4F (URL-encoded #B98A4F) inside the .year-sel SVG data URI (line 414), which the plain hex regex misses.
6 of the 98 (lines 3-4) sit in the header comment and are not rendered; the tokenizer should skip them.
No hsl()/hsla() and no named colors used as real colors in range (only 'transparent' for resets/tap-highlight and 'currentColor' on .info-i).
4 entries are #000 inside mask layers (lines 292-293, marquee bulbs): hue is irrelevant in a mask; role fixed, do not tokenize.

--ink does double duty: page ground AND the dark label on amber/maple fills (16 `color: var(--ink)` uses file-wide). --tunnel is used once the same way (.sort-chip.active). Those uses need to read var(--t-accent-ink) or a light theme breaks every amber button label.
--tunnel-2 (ground-3) is mostly used as a border (~21 border uses vs ~7 fills). A theme needs border uses split onto --t-line.
--maple (metal) doubles as the eyebrow/label text color and as a fill behind ink text (.slot-badge, .slot.filled, .tab.on, .ls-token). Repainting metal repaints all eyebrows.

The keycap palette (#E89A1C face / #F8B647 top / #9E5A0F side / #2A1A05 ink + white inset + black drop) is written twice: button.presti-spin group (232-260) and .donate-btn (934-958). Should become one shared set of --t-accent* tokens.

#E89A1C is the keycap FACE here (accent), although the spec lists it as an accent-edge example. It is oranger/deeper than --amber #FFB52E, so the keycap and flat amber fills (.confirm-btn, .btn-primary, .startover-btn, .sort-chip.active) are two different ambers today.
Refund (green) and fire-sale (red) keycap variants need hi/edge/ink roles the vocabulary lacks: good-hi, good-edge, good-ink, bad-hi. Mapped to good / accent-ink / bad with notes.

The Heat Check 'hot' reds (#ff5a4a text, #ff4133 border, rgba(255,65,51,a) glows; 13 entries) mean a POSITIVE bonus but were mapped to bad per the spec's examples. A `hot` role would let a theme keep losses and hot bonuses apart. Meanwhile .ledger-amt.hot uses --ok (green) for the same concept.
Disabled keycap colors (#6c6048 / #3a352a / #4a4434) are warm-tinted and have no `disabled` role; mapped text-2 / ground-3 / line.
#555c63 (.skip-btn:disabled, line 225) is likely dead CSS: .skip-btn always carries .presti-spin, and button.presti-spin:disabled (specificity 0,2,1) beats .skip-btn:disabled (0,2,0).

Not reachable from CSS variables: (1) the .year-sel chevron color, baked into a data: SVG URI (line 414); (2) .brand-logo = logo.png raster (index.html:81); (3) .crest-img team crest images; (4) .goat-particle emoji glyphs. JS in this range's classes only sets positions (tw-fill width, climb-pin top), not colors. app.js:1409-1411 builds an inline SVG with fill='var(--amber)' / stroke='var(--maple)', which IS reachable through the tokens.

Shape language in range: square corners almost everywhere (cards, tickets, rows, chips, tabs, inputs, badges); rounded only for keycaps (9px), .pool-search (8px), .share-out (4px), .ls-pos (7px), pills (.sort-chip, .ls-swap 999px), round tokens/dots (50%), tw-track (5px). Depth only on keycaps (5px solid extrusion + drop) and glow effects (amber halos, red hot glows).

Type: Barlow Condensed 700/800 for display numbers and names (ticket 40px, board big 64px, kaman up to 104px, intro 36px); IBM Plex Mono for every label, eyebrow, stat, chip, input; Barlow for running text and player names; Georgia italic only for the (i) info glyphs.
